requirement_text.REQ-372:
Filed from a GUI-review sweep applying "review real screens before writing a blind Playwright spec" to test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/definition-type-error-blocked.yaml (test/uat-reports/gui-review-2026-09-20-definition-type-error-blocked.md has the full trace). That scenario's own stale NOTE (ISS-0527) already flagged its pipeline_test as an aspirational forward-reference to a feature never built; this run verified that independently by reading current source rather than trusting the note, and confirms the underlying feature genuinely does not exist, in whole or in part.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, verified 2026-09-20 by direct source read (not inference): Letflow.Definitions.Graph.validate_edge_conditions/1 (REQ-029) checks structural edge-condition rules (default/condition conflicts, single-default-edge, and -- since REQ-288 -- real CEL grammar validity via Letflow.Engine.Expr.parse_strict/1). None of this resolves a variable NAME against anything: REQ-288's own docstring for the check it replaced states it "never resolves variable names," and REQ-288 itself only tightened syntax/grammar checking, explicitly out of scope for name resolution. Letflow.Engine.VariableSchema (REQ-109) stores each process's declared fields, but a grep of lib/ for any call cross-referencing an authored expression's variable references against VariableSchema returns zero hits outside REQ-291's x-ui vocabulary path (visible_when/computed/cross-field validation on FORM FIELDS only, docs/frontend/ x-ui vocabulary) -- REQ-291's own field-existence check does not run against EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge conditions or any task-routing/assignment rule. Letflow.Definitions.Graph.check_* node-attribute validators (REQ-029 CHK-09..12) require a HUMAN_TASK's "role" attribute to be a non-blank STRING, not an expression -- there is no mechanism today for a human-task assignment rule to reference a process field at all, so the scenario's "routes to a reviewer using a field the process does not hold" case has no code path to even reach. Nowhere in lib/letflow/ does any check compare the declared TYPE of two expression operands (e.g. a money-amount field against a customer-name field) -- Expr.parse_strict/1 is untyped; it validates syntax only. web/src's DefinitionEditorPage.tsx / ValidationSummaryBar / per-node canvas annotation plumbing is real and generic (any {nodeId|edgeId, message, severity} renders correctly, per-node annotations already exist for SUB_PROCESS interface errors, REQ-032), but nothing feeds it a field-existence or type-mismatch violation today, and there is no misspelled-field-name suggestion feature (grepped lib/ and web/src for did-you-mean/Levenshtein/nearest-field logic -- no hits).

THIS REQUIREMENT (backend half; a follow-on FRONTEND-DEV requirement, sized once this lands, wires the canvas/problem-list presentation -- same two-step shape as REQ-288 then REQ-291): build the semantic validation pass itself. Given a definition's graph and its VariableSchema-declared fields, for every authored rule expression (EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge condition at minimum; decide and record explicitly whether a HUMAN_TASK routing/assignment-by-field mechanism is in scope here or is its own prerequisite gap to file separately -- do not silently assume one way), report ALL violations in one pass (no fix-one-to-see-the-next), each violation naming the offending step/rule and the rule text as authored, for two rule classes: (1) a referenced variable name not present in the process's declared VariableSchema fields -- the violation must name the exact typed string and suggest the nearest declared field name (a real string-distance measure such as Levenshtein against the declared field list, not a placeholder); (2) a comparison between two operands whose declared VariableSchema types are not comparable (e.g. a money/numeric field against a text/string field) -- decide and record explicitly which type pairs are and are not comparable, rather than leaving the boundary implicit. This pass must re-run in full -- not read a cached prior result -- at whatever the definition's actual release/promotion submission call path is (verify at start which function that is; do not assume it is the same validate_definition_graph/2 the draft-save path uses without confirming).

Re-verify at start rather than trusting this description: the current shape of Letflow.Definitions.Graph.validate_edge_conditions/1's Violation struct and call sites (REQ-288 already extended these three: create/2, validate_update_graph/1 under update/2, validate_definition_graph/2 -- confirm they are unchanged), the exact declared-field type vocabulary VariableSchema currently supports, and whether any HUMAN_TASK routing-by-field mechanism has landed under a different name since this filing.

SCOPE FENCE: backend field-existence and type-compatibility checking, its violation shape (including the suggestion string), and re-running it at release-submission time. Does not build the frontend presentation (canvas problem markers, the problem-list UI, or the release-submission re-check screen) -- that is explicitly a follow-on FRONTEND-DEV requirement once this lands, filed the same way REQ-291 followed REQ-288. Does not extend Letflow.Engine.Expr's grammar (REQ-288's closed EXP-102 decision stands unchanged) -- this requirement adds a separate, subsequent semantic pass over an already-parsed expression's referenced names and operand types, not a grammar change.

task.description:
Produce the design artefact for REQ-372 at lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md, per WF-02 Step 1's procedure (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md). You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921 (verify with git branch --show-current before writing anything -- STOP and report FAIL if it isn't that). This is a BACKEND-ONLY requirement: design a new module only, no web/ presentation layer (that is an explicitly out-of-scope follow-on requirement).

Before designing, RE-VERIFY (do not trust the requirement text's own claims) by reading the actual current source: (a) Letflow.Definitions.Graph.validate_edge_conditions/1's Violation struct shape and its three call sites (create/2, validate_update_graph/1 under update/2, validate_definition_graph/2) -- confirm these are unchanged since REQ-288; (b) the exact declared-field type vocabulary Letflow.Engine.VariableSchema currently supports (it stores each variable as a JSON Schema document -- read variable_schema.ex directly to determine the real type vocabulary, e.g. JSON Schema 'type' values, rather than assuming a bespoke enum); (c) whether any HUMAN_TASK routing-by-field mechanism has landed under a different name since this requirement was filed (grep lib/letflow/ for anything resolving a HUMAN_TASK assignment/role attribute against a process field) -- if none exists, explicitly decide and record in the design (and instruct ELIXIR-DEV to record in the moduledoc) that a HUMAN_TASK routing/assignment-by-field mechanism is OUT OF SCOPE for this requirement (a separate prerequisite gap), with your stated reasoning; do not silently assume this without verifying; (d) what the definition's actual release/promotion submission call path is (read lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex and its router/context callers) -- do NOT assume it is the same validate_definition_graph/2 the draft-save path uses without confirming by reading the code; name the exact function(s) in your design.

Design a new semantic validation pass (a new module, e.g. Letflow.Definitions.SemanticValidation or similar -- your call, state your naming rationale) that, given a definition's Graph and its VariableSchema-declared fields, for every EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge condition expression: (1) detects every referenced variable name not present in the declared VariableSchema fields, producing a violation naming the exact typed variable name, the step/edge it belongs to, and a suggested nearest declared field name computed by a REAL string-distance measure (Levenshtein or equivalent -- design the exact algorithm/signature, not a placeholder); (2) detects every comparison between two operands whose declared VariableSchema types are not comparable, using an explicit comparable/non-comparable type-pair table you define and record in full (at minimum: numeric/money vs text/string must be recorded non-comparable) -- this table must appear in the design so REVIEWER and the moduledoc can be checked against it verbatim. ALL violations across both rule classes must be collected and returned together in a single pass (no early return on first violation). Design must specify: how the pass is invoked from the release/promotion submission path you identified in (d) so it always re-runs in full (never a cached prior result) -- design the exact call-site change; the Violation/result shape (reuse or extend Graph.Violation's shape -- your call, state which); full @spec-style signatures for every new public function; error/success shapes; how expression operand identification interacts with Letflow.Engine.Expr's ALREADY-PARSED AST (you must NOT propose any change to lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex's grammar/parser -- REQ-288's EXP-102 decision is closed; this is a separate pass consuming Expr's already-parsed output, e.g. walking the parsed AST to find identifier references and their comparison contexts -- if Expr's public API doesn't yet expose what you need read-only, state exactly what read-only accessor you need and confirm it needs no grammar change).

Open questions must be listed explicitly, not silently resolved by guessing. Every one of the requirement's 10 acceptance criteria (given in task.acceptance_criteria below) must map to a concrete design element -- state the mapping explicitly in the design doc's own section.

REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step-01b) FAILed this design on ONE dimension only -- everything else (all 10 ACs, the release/promotion call path choice, the type-pair table, the HUMAN_TASK-out-of-scope reasoning, zero expr.ex changes, and the deliberate create/2+update/2-left-unwired decision) was independently re-verified against source and confirmed sound; do not redo any of that. The single defect: lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md contains literal, copy-pasteable Elixir implementation code, which this gate fails on sight per WF-02 Step 1b check 2e (design artefacts carry signatures and type shapes only, never function bodies). Fix, narrowly: (1) Section 3.3's validate_definition_graph/2 -- currently a full function body with no 'described, not written' caveat (contrast with the correctly-written Section 3.2 treatment of run_semantic_validation/2) -- rewrite as a signature plus prose description of its behavior, exactly like Section 3.2's own pattern. (2) Section 3.2's activate/2 call-site change -- currently a literal case/end control-flow block -- rewrite as prose describing the call-site change (what gets called, where, and what the two outcomes are) plus the changed function's signature only, no case/do/end. (3) Section 3.2's two new interpret_activate_result/1 private clauses, each currently written with a literal 'do: error' body -- rewrite as a signature/behavior description (what each clause pattern-matches and what it returns), not literal clause bodies. Do not touch any other section. This is rework iteration 1 of max_rework 3. On completion, set this handoff's status to COMPLETED and result to a genuine first-hand PASS/FAIL report as normal.
acceptance_criteria: a definition whose EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge condition references a variable name absent from the definition's declared VariableSchema fields produces a violation naming the exact typed variable name and the step/edge it belongs to, proven by a test

that violation's message includes a suggested nearest declared field name, computed by a real string-distance measure (not a placeholder or first-alphabetical fallback), proven by a test with a clear one-typo case (e.g. 'cusotmer_name' when 'customer_name' is declared)

a definition comparing two operands of declared VariableSchema types this requirement records as non-comparable (at minimum: a numeric/money type against a text/string type) produces a violation, proven by a test; the comparable/non-comparable type-pair table is stated explicitly in the moduledoc, not left implicit

a definition with two independent broken rules (one field-existence violation, one type-compatibility violation) produces BOTH violations in a single validation call, proven by a test -- the author is never required to fix one to discover the other
a definition with zero semantic violations validates cleanly, proven by a test, including after both of the above violations are corrected in the same test

the semantic validation pass re-runs in full (not from a cached prior result) at the definition's actual release/promotion submission call path, proven by a test that changes the underlying VariableSchema or expression state between an earlier clean validation and the submission call, and asserts the submission call reflects the fresh state

whether a HUMAN_TASK routing/assignment-by-field mechanism is in scope for this requirement is stated explicitly in the moduledoc with the reasoning, not left for a reader to infer from what tests do or don't cover
git diff shows lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex unmodified, or if modified, modified only in ways that add no token/operator/builtin -- state which, per REQ-288's precedent
no file under web/ is modified by this requirement
mix letflow.check passes, with real output quoted

result.summary: REWORK ITERATION 1 complete. Fixed exactly the one defect step-01b's FAIL named -- literal, copy-pasteable Elixir implementation code in three places -- and touched nothing else in the document. (1) Section 3.3's validate_definition_graph/2: replaced the full literal `def ... with ... do ... end` function body with an @spec block plus a 'Change (described, not written)' prose paragraph describing the new with-chain step (fetch_schemas/3 call) and the fourth violations term appended to the existing three, matching the style already used correctly for run_semantic_validation/2 in section 3.2. (2) Section 3.2's activate/2 call-site change: replaced the literal `case run_service_scope_validator(...) do ... case run_semantic_validation(...) do ... end ... end` control-flow block with a 'Call-site change (described, not written)' prose paragraph naming what gets called, where (run_activate_transaction/4's :draft branch, between run_service_scope_validator/3 and activate_draft/3), and the two outcomes (ok falls through to activate_draft/3; error takes the branch's existing Repo.rollback(reason) path) -- no case/do/end anywhere. (3) Section 3.2's two new interpret_activate_result/1 private clauses: replaced the literal `defp interpret_activate_result(...), do: error` bodies with a bullet list describing each clause's match pattern and return value (pure pass-through, same shape as the existing {:service_scope_violation, _} / {:sequence_conflict, _} clauses), no literal clause syntax. No other section was touched: re-verification (§0), the new module's types/public function @specs (§1), the two semantic checks and the full type-pair table (§2), the create/2+update/2-left-unwired decision and its REVIEWER flag (§3.1), the HUMAN_TASK-out-of-scope reasoning (§4), the 6 open questions (§5), and the 10-AC mapping table (§6) are byte-identical to the prior iteration's content, only reformatted where the three fixes required it. Confirmed via grep of the updated file for `case .* do|do:|defp interpret|Repo\.rollback` as code (not prose) -- no matches outside prose sentences referencing the two outcomes by name.
issues: Flagged for REVIEWER in design §3.1: create/2 and update/2 (draft-save paths) are deliberately left unchanged by this design -- the new semantic checks gate only activate/2 (release) and are surfaced read-only via validate_definition_graph/2, diverging from REQ-288's own precedent of gating create/2+update/2 for CEL grammar validity. Justified by the UAT scenario's own step-by-step narrative (a broken draft still saves; only release/activation is blocked) but is a real behavioral choice, not free of judgment -- REVIEWER should confirm or override explicitly.

owned_modules in this handoff's context does not list lib/letflow/definitions.ex, but the call-site wiring this design requires (activate/2, validate_definition_graph/2, interpret_activate_result/1) necessarily lives there -- called out explicitly in design §3 so ELIXIR-DEV does not miss it.
